title: 佐治亚州长易手：首位黑人女州长，2028布局生变？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: getting with Keisha Lance Bottoms. She knew this is something that Stacey Abrams was not able to do.
segments.zh: 与凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯交流。她知道这是斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯未能做到的事。

segments.en: It is, and it's historic. She's the first black woman to be elected in the state of Georgia, and of course, she defeated a self-financed candidate
segments.zh: 确实如此，而且具有历史意义。她是佐治亚州首位当选的黑人女性，当然，她击败了一位自筹资金的候选人。

segments.en: who wasn't even the favored candidate in the primary of either the president or the governor, or in terms of Brian Kemp, Rick Jackson,
segments.zh: 这位候选人甚至不是总统或州长初选中的热门人选，也不是布莱恩·坎普或里克·杰克逊看好的候选人。

segments.en: but she had a really tough contest. And of course, this opens up the possibility of 2028.
segments.zh: 但她经历了一场非常艰难的竞选。当然，这为2028年创造了可能性。

segments.en: Yes, Kayleigh, I have to go there for John Asif.
segments.zh: 是的，凯莉，我必须为约翰·阿西夫提到这一点。

segments.en: I think it would have been, I'm sorry, Vic, it would have been really tough for him to even consider that, because she would now be in a position to name his replacement.
segments.zh: 抱歉，维克，我认为他甚至连考虑都会非常困难，因为她现在将有能力任命他的继任者。

segments.en: But also, let's not forget, this means Democrats now control, at least to the governorship, a key battleground state.
segments.zh: 但别忘了，这意味着民主党现在至少控制了州长职位，这是一个关键的摇摆州。

segments.en: And that is something that we are seeing sort of flag out across the country.
segments.zh: 这是我们看到在全国范围内逐渐显现的情况。

segments.en: That has ripple effects from 28, and also, of course, as we redistrict after the 2030 census.
segments.zh: 这将对28年产生影响，当然，还有2030年人口普查后的选区重划。

segments.en: Yeah, and that's one of the reasons we pay a lot of attention to Georgia.
segments.zh: 是的，这就是我们非常关注佐治亚州的原因之一。
